'''Robert Martin Edwards IV'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Robert Martin Edwards IV () - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/339893-robert-martin-edwards-iv |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=8 June 2025}}</ref> (born January 20, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Pallacanestro Reggiana|Reggio Emilia]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA). He played college basketball for the [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State Vikings]] and [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]] before beginning his professional career with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] in 2021. During the [[2021–22 NBA season|2021–22 season]], Edwards was called up to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

==Early life==
Edwards was born and raised in [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]].<ref name=csuvikings>{{cite web|url=https://www.csuvikings.com/sports/m-baskbl/2015-16/bios/edwards_rob_q2w5|title=Rob Edwards|work=csuvikings.com|access-date=December 28, 2021|archive-date=December 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228060807/https://www.csuvikings.com/sports/m-baskbl/2015-16/bios/edwards_rob_q2w5|url-status=dead}}</ref> He attended the [[University of Detroit Jesuit High School and Academy]] for the first two years of high school before transferring to [[Cass Technical High School]].<ref name="csuvikings"/> He helped Cass Tech to a Class A District title as a junior, scoring 19 points in the district championship game.<ref name="csuvikings"/> He earned honorable mention all-state honors as a senior in 2014–15, averaging 16 points, six rebounds, six assists and three steals per game.<ref name="csuvikings"/>

==College career==
Edwards played his first two years of [[college basketball]] for the [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State Vikings]].<ref name="csuvikings"/> He was named to the [[Horizon League]] All-Freshman Team in 2016<ref name="csuvikings"/> and second-team All-Horizon League in 2017.<ref name=realgm>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Rob-Edwards/Summary/85686|title=Rob Edwards|work=realgm.com|access-date=December 28, 2021}}</ref> Edwards averaged 16.5 points and 4.5 rebounds per game as a sophomore. He transferred to [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] following the season and sat out the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] due to NCAA transfer regulations.<ref>{{cite web|last=Decker|first=Ryan|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/1098632/report-cleveland-state-guard-rob-edwards-transfer-asu/|title=Report: Cleveland State guard Rob Edwards to transfer to ASU|work=arizonasports.com|date=April 22, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170424174528/https://arizonasports.com/story/1098632/report-cleveland-state-guard-rob-edwards-transfer-asu/|archive-date=April 24, 2017|access-date=December 28, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Metcalfe |first=Jeff |date=December 15, 2018 |title=Edwards back on court for Sun Devils |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99049627 |access-date=April 4, 2022 |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |page=6C |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref> As a redshirt junior, Edwards averaged 11.1 points and 3.3 rebounds per game. He averaged 11.6 points and 3.6 rebounds per game as a senior and scored a season-high 24 points twice.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gardner |first=Michelle |title=Former ASU star Rob Edwards selected by Thunder in G-League draft |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/asu/2021/01/12/former-asu-standout-picked-thunder-g-league-draft/6639066002/ |access-date=December 28, 2021 |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |date=January 12, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2021–2022)===
Edwards went undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref name="realgm"/> In January 2021, he joined the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League]] after being selected in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|G League draft]].<ref name="realgm"/><ref>{{cite web|last=Newman|first=Logan|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2021/01/11/okc-blue-select-lu-dorts-asu-teammate-rob-edwards-in-g-league-draft/|title=OKC Blue select Lu Dort's ASU teammate Rob Edwards in G League draft|work=okcthunderwire.usatoday.com|date=January 11, 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111223033/https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2021/01/11/okc-blue-select-lu-dorts-asu-teammate-rob-edwards-in-g-league-draft/|archive-date=January 11, 2021|access-date=December 28, 2021}}</ref> He played for the Blue in the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|G League hub season]] between February and March 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/player/rob-edwards/|title=Rob Edwards|work=gleague.nba.com|access-date=December 28, 2021}}</ref> In 15 games, he made three starts and averaged 12.5 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 21.3 minutes per game on 44.0 percent shooting from beyond the arc.<ref name=training-camp>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-trainingcamp-210927|title=Thunder Adds Edwards and Wilson to Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2021|access-date=December 28, 2021}}</ref>

In August 2021, Edwards played for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the [[2021 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]].<ref name="realgm"/> He signed with the Thunder on September 27,<ref name="training-camp"/> and was then waived on October 11 after appearing in one preseason game.<ref name="realgm"/><ref>{{cite web|last=Parker|first=Derek|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/thunder-waive-rob-edwards|title=Thunder Waive Guard Rob Edwards|work=si.com|date=October 11, 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211012020913/https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/thunder-waive-rob-edwards|archive-date=October 12, 2021|access-date=December 28, 2021}}</ref> He re-joined the Blue for the [[2021–22 NBA G League season]].<ref name="realgm"/> On December 27, 2021, he signed a 10-day contract with the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder-signs-three-211227|title=Thunder Signs Three Players to 10-Day Contracts|work=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2021|access-date=December 28, 2021}}</ref> He re-joined the Blue on January 6<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/transactions/league/2022|title=2021-2022 G League Transactions|work=realgm.com|access-date=January 8, 2022}}</ref> after appearing in two NBA games.<ref>{{cite news |last=Creider |first=Ben |date=January 8, 2022 |title=Stories From the G: Rob Edwards' Rise From Unranked Status to the League |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/stories-from-the-g-rob-edwards-rise-from-unranked-status-to-the-league |access-date=April 4, 2022 |work=[[FanNation]] |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref>

===Wisconsin Herd (2022–2023)===
On September 2, 2022, Edwards' returning rights were acquired by the [[Wisconsin Herd]] in a trade with the Blue.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2022 |title=OKC Blue announces G League trade that involves Javin DeLaurier and Rob Edwards |url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2022/09/03/okc-blue-announces-g-league-trade-that-involves-javin-delaurier-and-rob-edwards/ |access-date=September 17, 2022 |website=OKC Thunder Wire |language=en-US}}</ref> On September 16, he signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], but was waived on the same day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Transactions - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/transactions/league/2023 |access-date=September 17, 2022 |website=basketball.realgm.com}}</ref> On November 3, 2022, Edwards was named to the opening-night roster for the Herd.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2022-23-opening-day-roster/n-5895537|title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2022-23 Opening Day Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}}</ref> He averaged 15.1 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game during the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]].<ref name=bggoettingen>{{cite web|url=https://www.bggoettingen.de/edwards-verstaerkt-bg-im-saisonendspurt/|title=EDWARDS VERSTÄRKT BG IM SAISONENDSPURT|website=bggoettingen.de|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=April 2, 2023|language=German}}</ref>

===BG Göttingen (2023)===
On March 28, 2023, Edwards signed with [[BG Göttingen]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref name="bggoettingen"/>

===Cleveland Charge (2023)===
On October 21, 2023, Edwards was signed and immediately waived by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Cavaliers Waive Seven Players|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/cavaliers-waive-seven-players.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}}</ref> He subsequently joined the [[Cleveland Charge]] of the [[NBA G League]] for the [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2023 Training Camp Roster|url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}}</ref> In 16 Showcase Cup games, he averaged 9.9 points in 16 games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rob Edwards|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Rob-Edwards/Summary/85686|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 25, 2024}}</ref>

===Maine Celtics (2023–2024)===
On December 26, 2023, Edwards was traded to the [[Maine Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maine Acquires Rob Edwards In Three-Team Trade|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/rob-edwards-signs-122623|website=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2023|access-date=January 14, 2024}}</ref> He was waived on February 24, 2024,<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Maine Celtics Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Maine-Celtics/64/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 25, 2024}}</ref> after averaging 6.5 points in 16 games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rob Edwards stats |url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1630306 |access-date=February 25, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Delaware Blue Coats (2024)===
On March 4, 2024, Edwards joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Blue Coats add Edwards to their roster|url=https://www.usbasket.com/NBA-G-League/news/857389/Blue-Coats-add-Edwards-to-their-roster|website=USBasket.com|date=March 4, 2024|access-date=March 4, 2024}}</ref>

===Cairns Taipans (2024–2025)===
On May 24, 2024, Edwards signed with the [[Cairns Taipans]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2024–25 NBL season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster heats up with Rob Edwards|url=https://www.taipans.com/news/roster-heats-up-with-rob-edwards|website=Taipans.com|date=May 24, 2024|access-date=May 24, 2024}}</ref> On November 6, he received a one match suspension for his actions and comments towards referees after a game against [[Melbourne United]] on October 27.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rob Edwards sanction handed down |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/rob-edwards-sanction-handed-down |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=November 6, 2024 |date=November 6, 2024}}</ref> On February 2, 2025, he was granted an early release from his contract to allow him to depart for his next destination. He averaged 19.8 points, 4.1 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game.<ref name=nbl>{{cite news |title=Edwards to depart Taipans early |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/edwards-to-depart-taipans-early |access-date=February 2, 2025 |work=NBL Official Website |date=February 2, 2025}}</ref>

===Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2025)===
On February 4, 2025, Edwards joined the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA) for the rest of the [[2024–25 Chinese Basketball Association season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=罗伯特·爱德华兹已完成注册 |url=https://weibo.com/1828625142/PdnFna0LR |website=微博 |access-date=February 8, 2025 |date=February 8, 2025 |quote=爱德华兹已于2月4日到队}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=完成注册！罗伯特·爱德华兹加入新疆男篮 |url=https://www.ts.cn/xwzx/tyxw/202502/t20250208_26608290.shtml |website=天山网 |access-date=February 10, 2025 |date=February 8, 2025}}</ref> In five games, he averaged 7.6 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game.<ref name=Eurobasket>{{cite web |title=Rob Edwards |url=https://basketball.asia-basket.com/player/Rob-Edwards/370757 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=20 January 2026 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===Osos de Manatí (2025)===
Edwards played six games for [[Osos de Manatí]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] during the [[2025 Baloncesto Superior Nacional season|2025 season]], averaging 10.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game.<ref name="Eurobasket" />

===Jiangsu Dragons (2025)===
In December 2025, Edwards joined the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the Chinese Basketball Association. He appeared in six games between December 13 and December 30.<ref name="Eurobasket" />

===Hangzhou Jingwei (2026)===
In January 2026, Edwards joined [[Hangzhou Jingwei]] of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]]. In 20 games, he averaged 15.2 points, 4.5 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.2 steals per game.<ref name="Eurobasket" />

===Ironi Kiryat Ata (2026)===
In May 2026, Edwards joined [[Ironi Kiryat Ata B.C.|Ironi Kiryat Ata]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]]. In six games to finish the [[2025–26 Israeli Basketball Premier League|2025–26 season]], he averaged 21.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.7 steals per game.<ref name="Eurobasket" />

===Pallacanestro Reggiana (2026–present)===
On July 16, 2026, Edwards signed with [[Pallacanestro Reggiana|Reggio Emilia]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite Instagram |user=pallacanestroreggiana |postid=Da0wW1OF1GN |title=Rob Edwards è un nuovo giocatore della Pallacanestro Reggiana |date=July 21, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Edwards has one brother and one sister. His cousin, [[Kalin Lucas]], played basketball at [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] and played in the NBA in 2014 and 2019.<ref name="csuvikings"/>

Edwards has a daughter who was born in 2024.<ref name=nbl/>
